sections.label: Respiratory
sections.text:
Nose dry. Tickling in throat-pit
causes cough. Copious mucous discharge from nose and
trachea. Dry. teasing cough, preventing sleep. Aggra-
vated by pressure, talking, and especially by inspiring
cool air and at flight. Thin, watery, frothy expectora-
tion by the mouthful; later, stringy and tough. Raw-
ness of larynx and trachea. Soreness behind sternum,
especially left side, in region of left shoulder. Raw
pain under clavicle. Lump in throat.

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Vertigo (within half an hour), 7 '.—Vertigo with the nausea
(tenth day), 2 .—Dizziness several times (first day), 9 .—[10.] Rose in the
morning with slight feeling of oppression in head (third day), 2b .—A heavy
feeling in head, during the evening (first day), 2 *.—Fulness in the head,
with the feeling of languor (second day), 8 .—Feeling of languor and uni¬
versal heaviness, with fulness in the head and chest (half an hour after
second dose, second day), 8 .—Dull heavy feeling in head, during the even¬
ing (seventh day), 2 .—Dull heavy headache, accompanied with deepseated
soreness of eyes, during the day, worse in the forenoon (fourteenth and fif¬
teenth days), lb .—Dull heavy headache, from 10 a.m. until night; not so

severe after 2 p.m.; disappeared at night (second day), 1 .—A dull heavy head¬
ache during the day, less severe in the afternoon (second day) ; dull heavy
headache during the day (third day), la .—A dull heavy headache, with deep-
seated soreness of the eyes most of the day (second day), 1 '.—Dull headache
during the forenoon (seventh, eighteenth, and twenty-fifth days), 1 '.—[20.]
A great deal of dull heavy headache during the day (tenth day), 1 '.—Dull
heavy headache through the day (fourteenth day) ; during the forenoon
(fifteenth day), 1 '—Dull headache followed the sharp pain and rumbling in
the abdomen, in the evening (twenty-fourth), 1 '.—Some headache accom¬
panied the pain in the lungs, 1 '.—The headache mentioned in Rumex crispus
is increased by motion, 1 '.—Headache all the forenoon (tenth day), 9 .—Slight
headache after retiring late at night (seventh day), 2 .—Slight headache 1 ;
(third, thirteenth, and twenty-third days), 1 '; (fourth day),’\—Pain in the
head on movement (tenth day), 3 .—Headache, with coryza, 7 .—[30 ] Slight
pain in head before breakfast (second day), 3 '.—The head began to ache,
and ached severely until going to sleep, towards midnight (after three
hours) ; the headache returned on waking, and continued until noon, next
day; it was dull (third day); very severe (fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth,
and ninth days) ; continued the whole forenoon (tenth day); affects most
frequently the temples ; is felt in the occiput (sixth and eighth days) ; over
the right eye (sixth and seventh day); in the forehead (twelfth day), 9 .—
Awoke with a bruised sensation in the brain, increased by moving, stoop¬
ing, and by any sudden movement of the head. This bruised sensation
continued until noon, and suddenly disappeared after dinner (seventh day)/ 3 .
— Forehead. Dull bruised feeling in the forehead, most severe in the
right side of the forehead, worse when moving the head, when it feels as if
the brain were loose for a few minutes (first day) ; continued until morning,
when it was worse than last evening (second morning), 8 ®.— *Dull headache
and slight bruised feeling in the forehead, nearly all day (fourth day), 8a .—
Dull headache in the forehead, with heat and redness of the face, after
singing, in the evening (fifth day) ; entirely relieved, after sixth dose, 8a .—■
Dull aching pain through the whole forepart of the head, at 11 a.m. (fourth
day), 3 ®.—Dull aching in the forehead attended the toothache (after three
hours, second day), 8 .—Slight dull pain in the frontal region, with indispo¬
sition to thought (after one hour, fourth day), 2 .—Frontal headache, with
the feverish symptoms (tenth morning), 2 .—[40.] Fulness and aching
through the front part of the head and temples (three hours after second
dose, second day), 8 .—Headache in forehead, increased soon after fourth
dose, connected with a pungent tingling sensation in the occiput, where
phrenologists locate philoprogenitiveness/*.—Pain over right eyebrow, with
sensation of stoppage in left ear (after one hour and a quarter), 7 '.—Sen¬
sation across the forehead, as if the brain were loose, when moving the
head, and as if it were bruised; this continued until after breakfast, next
morning (after two minutes), 8 .—Pain over right eyebrow (after one hour), 7 ';
(sixth day), 1 '.—Pain on the right side of the forehead in the region of
causality (after one hour and fifty minutes, seventeenth day), 5 .—Slight
frontal headache, with shooting pains, at 7.30 p.m. (tenth day); slight
frontal headache (twelfth day), 2 *.—Slight frontal headache, increased by
motion (fourteenth day), 2 .—Slight aching pain in the forehead, at 9 p.m.
(second day), 30 .—A sharp pain in the forepart of the head, in the open air
(sixth day), 5 .— Temples. [50.] Pain in right temple, then iu the left
(fifth day), 9 .—Pain iu the right temple (seventh day); in the mornino-
(eighth day), 9 .—Severe pain for an hour in right temple (twelfth day), 9 .—


419

Dull aching pain in the left temple (one hour after second dose, second day), 8 .
—Pain in left temple (after one hour), 7 '; in the afternoon, 9 .— Vertex and
JParietals, Aching and pressure in the top of the head (one hour after
second dose, second day), 8 .—Sharp pain, piercing, in the left side of the
head, for a short time (after three hours, second day), 8 .—A darting pain in
left side of head, for about half an hour, at 11 a.m. and 8 p.m. (third day), 3 ".
— Occiput. Dull aching pain low iu the occiput (one hour after second
dose, second day), 8 .—A dull aching pain in the occiput, which comes and
goes, in the afternoon (eleventh day), 5 .— [ 60 .] Pungent drawing pain in
the left side of the occiput, with a similar pain in the left nostril, and a
feeling as if coryza would ensue (eighteen hours after second dose), 8 *.

Eye .—Pains in both eyes, more severe iu the right (after three hours), 9 .
—Pains in both eyes, heavy and dull (second day), 9 .—Pains over the left
and in both eyes, with soreness to the touch over left (fourth day), 9 .—Pains
in or over either or both eyes (fifth and sixth days), 9 .—Pains in either eye
(seventh day), 9 .—Pains in the right eye, and in both (ninth and tenth
days), 9 .—Pain iu the right eye, both eyes all the forenoon (tenth day), 9 .—
Pains in right eye, deepseated (third day), 9 .—Pains in the right eye (eighth,
ninth, tenth, and eleventh days), 9 .— [ 70 .] Pains dull and steady in the
right eye (after three hours), 9 .—Pains sharp, shooting, in the left eye, run¬
ning to the right jaw and arm (after three hours), 9 .—Pain over the left
eye, with soreness to touch (fifth day), 9 .—For several nights eyes have felt
somewhat sore, as if the eyelids were inflamed and dry, particularly in
evening, though no external signs of inflammation present themselves (fif¬
teenth day), 2b .—Lachrymation (sixth day), 9 .

Ear .—Pain in both ears (seventh day), 9 .—Pain in right ear (third and
sixth days); repeatedly (seventh day), 9 .—Pain in the right ear, in the
morning (eighth, ninth, and eleventh days), 9 .—Pain in the left ear and
running to the shoulder (fourth day), 9 .—Pain in left ear (fifth day), 9 .—
[ 80 .] Pain in the left ear, in the afternoon (eighth day), 9 .—Boring pain
just behind the base of the left ear (two hours after second dose, second
day), 8 .—Heavy throbbing in the ears, synchronous with the pulsations of
the heart, attended the stinging, almost itching, pain iu the left side of
the chest (after one hour, fourth day), 8 . — Sensation of stoppage iu left
ear, with pain over right eyebrow (after one hour and a quarter), 7 '.—Sen¬
sation as if the ears were obstructed, especially the left one; the prover’s
own voice (as well as the voices of others) sounds strangely to him, pro¬
ducing a kind of titillation in the ear, and having a peculiar ringing con¬
fusing sound, and yet the sense of hearing is as acute as ever; continued
eighteen hours (after six hours, sixth day); still continues, but not to so
great a degree; attended by slight ringing in the ears, at 10 p.m. (eighth
day), 8 .—Constant roaring in the left ear, as if a conch-shell were held before
it, the whole day, attended by a feeling as if a fine thread were tied tightly
around the neck just below the ears; the roaring is not relieved by press¬
ing the finger into the ear; this continued for a week, and then gradually
disappeared (after nine days), 8 .—Ringing in the ears, 7 * 7b .

ness in the nose, the whole day and night (fifth day), 8 .—Dull pain in the

[100.] Great paleness of face while standing (tenth day), 2 .—
Pain in the side of the face, including the right temple and ear; also left

—Pain in right jaw, in the morning (eighth day), 9 .—Pain in the right
jaw and molar teeth (first day), 9 .—After retiring late at night had lanci¬
nating pains in lower jaw, at root of left caniue tooth (seventh day), 2 .

sections.text:
Teeth. Pain in the teeth of both sides, in the morning; in
the front teeth in the afternoon (ninth day), 9 .—Dull aching pain in the
right molars, both upper and lower, which is entirely relieved after eating
dinner (third day), 8a .—Severe dull aching in the right molars; relieved by
rinsing the mouth with cold water (tenth day), 8 *.—Grumbling-stinging
toothache in the l ight superior molars, while riding in a cold wind, attended
with a dull aching in the forehead (after three hours, second day), 8 .—[HO.]
Dull transient paip in teeth (fourth day), 2 .—Pain in the under jaw and
teeth, in the frout teeth, also on the left side, half an hour (eleventh day), 9 .—
Pain in the teeth, in the morning (eighth day), 9 .—Pain in the teeth of
lower jaw of left side (seventh day), 9 .—Running pains in teeth ; in all the
upper teeth (twelfth day), 9 .—Sharp pain in the teeth (second day), 9 .—
Tariff ue. Tongue coated white, with the feverish symptoms (tenth morn¬
ing), 1 *.-■—* Tongue coated yellow (tenth and seventeenth days), 5 .—Tongue
heavily coated (second and fifth days), 9 .—Feeling of dryness of the anterior
part of the tongue, with a feeling in the stomach of repletion, and as if
one had eaten spice (seventh day), 0 .—[120.] The anterior part of the tongue
felt dry and hot (after forty minutes), 5 .—Soreness of the right edge of the
tongue (after one hour and fifty minutes), 5 .—Sensation of excoriation at
edges of the tongue, which is sore when touched by the teeth, with a feel¬
ing as if the anterior part of the tongue had been scalded (twelfth day), 5 .—
Sensation as if the tongue and mouth were burnt, with the flatulency, 71 .—
Dryness of the mouth and tongue, at night (fourth day), 8 .— Saliva
anil Taste. Flow of saliva (within half an hour), 70 .—Rose in the morn¬
ing with bad taste in the mouth (third day), 25 .—Woke with a bitter taste
in the mouth (second day ), 21 .—Nasty taste in the mouth (second day), 9 .—
Flat taste in the mouth, on rising, in the morning, was quite frequent dur¬
ing the proving, 10 .

[140.] Tickling in the throat, soon after taking the drug, then throat a
little sore (fifth day), 9 .— Fauces and Pharynx. Much tough mucus
in the fauces, which is very difficult to eject (seventh day), 8a .—Aching in
the pharynx, and collection of tough mucus in the fauces, with a slight
inclination to cough, in the evening (fifth day), 8 *.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Appetite and Thirst. Appetite much increased;
feels hungry even alter a full meal (fifteenth day), 2 .—Less appetite than
usual (seventh day), 2 —Anorexia (eighth and twelfth days), 9 .—Loss of
appetite and nausea, 4b . — At 7.30 p.m. was very thirsty, though this is un¬
usual to him (fourth day), 2 .—Thirsty during evening (eighth day), 2 .—
Eructations ■ Belching of wind accompanied the pain in the lungs,''.—
[ 150 .] Eructation, empty, 78 .—Eructation (within half an hour), 7 ®.—Eruc¬
tation and sensation of distension in the stomach ; the feeling of distension
subsides with motion of wind in the bowels, 7b .—Eructation of wind (after
ten minutes), ,a .—Frequent forcible eructation of tasteless flatus, in the
evening (fifth day), 8 *.—Eructation of much tasteless flatus, with a sensation
of distension in the scrobiculus cordis (a quarter of an hour after second
dose, second day), 8 .— Hiccough. Hiccough (after one hour), 7 ®.—Pyrosis
after dinner (sixth day), 9 .— Nausea and Vom iting. Nausea and loss
of appetite (sixth day), 48 .—In the evening nausea, relieved by eructations,
with sensation of fulness in the abdomen, as if diarrhoea was forming (fifth
day), 0 .— [ 160 .] Nausea; fulness of the stomach, with eructations with the
taste of what had been eaten, on going to bed (ninth day), 5 .—In the morn¬
ing, on awaking, felt nauseated, with moving in the intestines as from a
cathartic (second day), 4 .—Slight nausea (eighth day), 25 .—Slight nausea
while dressing, in the morning, and vertigo, compelling to lie down again
(tenth day), 2 .— Stomach. Awoke with an acid stomach and eructations
of acid flatus (fifth morning), 48 .—Weight in the stomach, like that which
is produced by the pressure of undigested food, with a pressing sensation
as far upwards as the throat-pit; this sensation continued for one hour
until falling asleep (after ten minutes, first day), 4 .—Weight in the epigas¬
trium like that of the previous night, but not so great, though no food had
been taken (after ten minutes, second day), 4 .—For two hours after first
dose experienced a sensation as of a hard substance in pit of stomach (third
day), 3< *.—*For several days an unusual sensation of heaviness in the epigas¬
trium; it occurs immediately after eating , and disappears in the course of
half an hour, 3 *.— *Feeling in the stomach of repletion and as if one had
eaten spice, with the feeling of dryness of the tongue (seventh day), 5 .—
[ 170 .] Fasted all day until evening, feeling empty and sunken, but with¬
out appetite (tenth day), 2 .—Previous sensation of undigested food returned
(after three hours, first day); same pressure in stomach continued through
afternoon, but disappeared in the night (first day), 45 .—Sensation of undi¬
gested food in the stomach, with upward pressure to the throat-pit; every
empty swallowing carried it downward towards the stomach, but it imme¬
diately returned (after fifteen minutes, second day), 4a .—Sensation as of a
hard body, somewhat increased after food, and continued for four hours
(second day); same sensation as of a hard body in the stomach, ascending
upwards to the throat-pit; the sensation at the throat-pit descended towards
the stomach upon every empty swallowing, but immediately returned; con¬
tinued for two hours, but gradually abated ; returned after dinner and
continued for two hours or more (after eight minutes, fifth day), 4 .—Severe
pain in the digestive organs on waking, in the morning, and frequent (fifth
day), 9 .—Pains severe in the gastric region (third day), 9 .—Pain dull and

422


heavy toward the cardiac orifice (fourth day), 9 .—Pains severe in the stom¬
ach (eighth day), 9 .— Pain in stomach on waking (eleventh day), 9 . Two
hours after breakfast felt as though his food had not digested (second and
third days), 2 .— [ 180 .] Pain in the stomach accompanied the pain in the
lungs, Ic .—Dull pains in stomach (seventh day), 29 .—A burning pain in the
pit of the stomach, for a short time (soon after first dose), 3b .—During the
day a burning pain in the stomach and abdomen (fourth day)," 8 .—A cut¬
ting pain in pit of stomach, for five minutes, while riding in the open air
(half an hour after first dose), 3 .—Acute momentary pain in the pit of the
stomach (fourth day), 39 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Pain above umbilicus (within half an bour), 7c .—Sensa¬
tion of distension in the scrobiculus cordis, with eructation of much taste¬
less flatus (a quarter of an hour after second dose, second day), 8 .—Dull
pain and sensation of fulness, as if from flatus, in the left side of the abdo¬
men, about midway between the umbilicus and crest of the ilium, while
riding; continued two hours (after three hours and a half, second day), 8 .—
Frequent passages of small quantities of fetid flatus (seventh night), 30 .—
[190.] Much flatus moving about in the abdomen, during the night (twenty-
second day), 3c .—Borborygmus (within half an hour), 7 '.—After meals flatu¬
lency (sixth day), 5 .—Flatulency in the morning on waking, with emission
of flatus, and sensation as if the tongue and mouth were burnt, 78 .—Rum¬
bling in the bowels and colic pains above the hypogastrium (fifth day)/ b .—
Rumbling in the bowels and eructation of wind, 7 .—Rumbling in the
bowels, with yawning (after one hour and ten minutes), 70 .—A relaxed sen¬
sation, with rumbling, continued for some hours, as if another evacuation
would follow, nevertheless it passed'off without another stool (fourth morn¬
ing), 41 '.—Moving in the intestines, with nauseous feeling, in the morning on
awaking (second day), 4 .—Sensation of fulness of abdomen on going to bed
(ninth day), 5 .—[200.] Sensation of fulness in the abdomen, as if diarrhoea
was forming, with the nausea (fifth day), 5 .—Towards evening an aching
pain commencing in the right side of the umbilicus (tenth day), 5 .—Dull
pain in the abdomen, in the evening (seventeenth day), Ic .—A dull pain
in the abdomen before rising; it continued a short time after rising, and
was followed by a diarrhoeic stool (third day),’ 0 .—*Awoke the next morn¬
ing with pain in the bowels; relieved by emission of flatus, 7 .—Pain in the
abdomen, about the seventh rib, on the right side; a gone feeling and a
weakness on each side of the umbilicus; the pains about 5 p.m., 6 . —^Griping
pain in the bowels, below the umbilicus, which is partially relieved by dis¬
charge of very offensive flatus, after breakfast (fifth day), 8 *.—Movement of
bowels, as if an evacuation would occur (after one hour and one-third), 7c .—
In the night woke with a pain all over the abdomen ; it was excessively
painful (tenth day), 5 .—Pain wandering over the belly (tenth day), 5 .—
L210.] Sensation in the bowels as if diarrhoea would ensue, with aching
pain in the rectum (one hour after second dose), 89 .—Sensation in the bowels
and rectum as if diarrhoea would ensue; continued two or three hours
(twenty-two hours after fifth dose), 8 .—Sensation in the bowels as if diarrhoea
would ensue, with aching in the rectum (fourth day), 8a .—During the day a
burning pain in the abdomen and stomach (fourth day), 31 .—A cutting pain
in the abdomen, in the evening, followed by a diarrhoeic stool (seventh
day), lb .—Sharp pain in the abdomen followed the symptoms of fever, and
was increased by deep inspiration, but entirely subsided on rising (second
morning), 18 .—Sharp pain and rumbling in the abdomen, in the evening,
followed by dull headache (twenty-fourth day), 10 .—Sharp pain in the lower


423

part of the abdomen, in the morning before rising, followed by two diar-
rhoeic stools, and a dull pain in the abdomen, which lasted two or three
hours (sixth day), 10 .

Rectum and Anns.—On retiring at night, first became aware of
the protrusion of a small hsemorrhoidal tumor (eleventh day); troubled
much all day, in all postures, by haemorrhoids; sensation of heat and irri¬
tation about the anus, with sensation as of a foreign body there (twelfth
day) ; hsemorrhoidal tumor still exists, but is slight ; itching of anus (four¬
teenth day) ; great itching of anus (seventeenth day), 2 .—Aching in the
rectum, with the sensation as if diarrhoea would ensue (fourth dav), 8a .—
[220.] A feeling in the rectum as if a rough stick was forced up. painful
on walking, in the evening (second day), 5 .—Itching in the anus, 7 .

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Diarrhoea. Copious diarrhoeic stool, with colic pains just
above the hypogastrium, and a very disagreeable rumbling in the bowels,
together with nausea and loss of appetite. These sensations continued
nearly throughout the day, with some four or five evacuations, which poured
away in a stream, as if a large quantity would be discharged ; nevertheless,
each discharge was suddenly arrested, and the inclination passed away en¬
tirely for a short time; but on rising the urgency returned, and on return-
, ing to the cabinet a new stream of liquid faeces poured forth as before.
At short intervals there occurred, throughout the day, inclination to go to
stool, with much rumbling of the bowels, but the urgency to stool was not
so pressing that it could not be well resisted (fifth day), 4b .— *In the morning
looseness of boivels, with colic some time before their movement; stool of brown
color (third day), 5 .—At the usual hour a very loose diarrhoeic discharge
from the bowels occurred (fourth morning), 45 .—*Movement of the bowels,
in the morning, watery and brown (tenth day), 5 .— *At 4 p.m. had a slight
liquid motion from bowels, the desire therefor being very urgent, and waking
him from sleep (fifteenth day), 2 ".—Motion of the intestines, with emission
of wind, 75 .—Faeces black (eleventh day) ; normally yellow (twelfth day), 2 .
—Scanty faeces (thirteenth day), 2 *.—[230.] Dry and hard stool (thirteenth
day), 10 .— Constipation, Previous to the taking of this medicine the
bowels were regular, but during the proving of it they were more or less
constipated, 15 . — * Constipation (eighth day); third day of constipation
(eleventh day), 9 .—Costiveness for three days (sixth day), 10 .—Constipation
for three days, followed by a natural stool (ninth day), 10 .—Constipation for
three days, follow'ed by a small dry and hard stool (sixteenth day), 10 .—
Constipation for three days, followed by a dry and hard stool (twenty-
fourth day), 10 .

Urinary Organs. —Constant inclination to urinate (sixth day), 9 . —
Frequent desire to urinate during the day (seventh day)/ 0 .—Inclination
to urinate not as frequent to-day as yesterday, but an unusual urgency with
the desire to urinate; must speedily evacuate the bladder, or there is a
sensation as if the urine could not be retained (eighth day); during the
dav noticed an urgency as soon as there is an inclination to urinate (nine¬
teenth day); same urgency; sensation as if the urine must be immediately
voided as soon as the inclination takes place, as if it would be impossible
to retain it long ; the sensation is apparently located at the neck of the
bladder (twentieth day); urgency as soon as there is an inclination to
urinate, which is rather too often (twenty-seventh day); urging to urinate
(twenty-eighth day)/ 0 .— [240.] During the day observed a frequent inclin¬
ation to urinate, attended with a sensation as if the urine could not long be
retained (fourth day)/ d .—Copious discharge of colorless urine (after eight

424


hours, second day), 8 .—In afternoon urine less copious than usual, red and
turbid, with a flocculent deposit and oily surface (eighth day); brickdust
sediment in urine very marked and heavy (ninth day), 2 .

Sexual Ovf/ans. —Tendency to phimosis (twelfth day), 21 .—During
evening had feeling of soreness and excoriation, with redness of end of
prepuce (ninth day); still soreness, with increased redness and itching
(tenth day), 21 .—Redness and soreness of prepuce, worse in evening and
early morning (eleventh day) ; itching of prepuce (twelfth day), 2 *.—Itch¬
ing of prepuce (twelfth and fifteenth days), 2 .—Sexual desire diminished
through the proving/ 1 .—Complete loss of sexual desire for several days
(sixth day), 8 .

j Respiratory Organs .— Larynx. *Much tough mucus in the
larynx, with a constant desire to hawk and raise it, but without relief; worse
at night, but has been troublesome all day (third day), 81 .— [ 250 .] *Secretion
of mucus in the larynx, removed by hawking (within half an hour),' 0 .—-
* Hawking up mucus from the larynx ?.—* Violent irritation to cough in the
larynx while eating; observed at three meals (third day)/ 1 . — * Pain in the
top of larynxTM.—*Pain in larynx (after one hour and one-third)/'. —*Pain
in the larynx, mostly on the left side ?.— Voice. At 2 p.m., on these two
consecutive days, the voice suddenly rose several notes in pitch, and so con¬
tinued for about half an hour; voice sounded at 4 p.m. as though he bad a
cold in his head (fourth day), 2 .—Obstruction of voice and some coryza
(fifth day), 2 .—Voice changed at 11 a.m. into a nasal tone, for a short time
only (second day)/ 1 . —* Hoarseness (tenth day)/.— Coagll. [ 260 .] In
three days he was attacked with a severe and durable cough, presenting a
character entirely different from any he had ever experienced. It was a
dry spasmodic cough, assimilating an early stage of whooping-cough. It
was dry at first, came on in paroxysms, preceded by a tickling sensation
in the throat-pit, and attended with congestion and slight pain in the head
and wrenching pains in the right side of the chest. The time of commencement
of the most violent paroxysm was a few minutes after lying down at night,
which was usually about 11 o’clock. This paroxysm lasted ten or fifteen min¬
utes; after this he slept all night. A less severe paroxysm occurred in bed, in
the morning, after waking, and at various times through the day. This state
continued about two weeks, when there was a commencement of expectora¬
tion of adhesive mucus in small quantities, detached with difficulty. The whole
duration was about a month. Some medicines were taken in the latter
stages, but without obvious effects, 10 . —*Hacking cough (after tw r elve min¬
utes)/ 1 .— Respiration. *Sensation of breathlessness, as if the air did not
penetrate the chest, or like what is felt when falling or passing very rapidly
through the air,TM.

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
* He has had a dull aching pain in the anterior portion of both
lungs, which has harassed him day and night, for the last five days; it was
accompanied with some headache and pain in the stomach, also with belching
of wind (thirty-fifth day)/'.—Aching pain in the anterior portion of the
lungs, which disappeared and returned several times, in the afternoon (sev¬
enteenth day ), lb .—* At 3.30 p.m., while writing at the desk, experienced for a
little time, five stitches in the substance of the left lung (sixth day)/ 0 .—
Fulness in the chest, with the feeling of languor (second day)/.—Raw pain
in the chest just under each clavicle, while hawking mucus out of the
throat (seventh day)/ 1 .— *Pain in chest (fifth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh
days), 9 .—Momentary shooting pains in various parts of the chest, during
the evening (twenty-seventh day), 3 '.—[270.] A deep inspiration causes


425

stitches around the waist, at 7 a.m. (third day'), 3 *.—Pain in chest, on both
sides (fourth day), 9 .— Front and Sides . *At one time in the afternoon,
while riding, a deep inspiration produced a very acute stitch along the left
margin of the sternum (third day), 3 *.—Sensation of dry heat in the middle
of the chest, with the stinging-burning pain in the back (sixth day), 8 .—
*Pain in right side; in the left side (sixth, seventh, and eighth days), 9 .—
* Severe pain in both sides, and felt as if in the lungs (third day), 9 .—*Pain in
right side of thoracic region when lying down ; left side, with sense of de¬
pression in the thorax (first and second days), 9 .—Pain a little below and
anterior to the nipple, most frequently on the right side of the chest, 7 .—
Pain in the right side about the lower rib, being like a bruised sensation
(after one hour and fifty minutes), 5 .—Burning-tingling pain (similar to
itching) below, and to the right of the left nipple (after six hours, second
day), 8 .— r 280.] Momentary sharp pain in right side of chest (fifteenth
day), 2 .—Dull pain in the left side near the back, just above the last true
rib, after lying down at night (eighth and ninth days), 8 *.— * Observed, a sore¬
ness for a few minutes in the whole of the left side of the chest, after turning to
that side (second day), 3 *. —*Pain in the left side of chest ,TM.— * Acute lancinat¬
ing pain, a little to the left of the sternum and under the left breast (four hours
and a half after second dose, sixth day), 3 *.—While at dinner, a momentary
slight stitch in the left side, near lower edge of the ribs (seventh day), 3 *.—
*A sticking pain in the left thoracic region, in the morning before rising, fol¬
lowed by a dull pain in the lungs (fourth day), 1 *.—* Paw stinging pain a little
to the left of the longitudinal centre of the sternum, which obstructs deep inspi¬
ration, at night (seventh day), 8a .—* Burning-stinging pain in the left side,
near the heart, came on soon after lying down in bed; gradually moved up
into the great pectoral muscle, about two inches above and to the left of the
nipple, and continued for a long time ; increased by a, deep inspiration and by
lying on the back or right side; relieved by lying on the left side (tenth day), 8 *.
—* Burning-stinging pain in the whole left side of the chest, suddenly, when
talcing a deep inspiration, while in the act of lying down in bed, at night (after
fourteen hours, third day), 8 .— [290.] * Stinging, almost itching pain in the
left side of the chest, just below the nipple, followed and accompanied the sting¬
ing-burning pain in the back; attended by heavy throbbing in the ears,
synchronous with the pulsations of the heart (after one hour, fourth day), 8 .
—* Burning pain, in the left side of the chest, just below the nipple, worse when
taking a deep inspiration (fifth day), 8 .—Sensation in the left chest, as if the
heart suddenly ceased beating; followed by a heavy throbbing through the
chest; this symptom has been felt several times since the beginning of this
proving (sixth day), 8 .—Great pressure and sense of depression in the upper
part of the breast (third day), 9 .—Very sharp pain in the breast, running
to the right and left (third day), 9 .—Sharp pain in the breast (sixth, sev¬
enth, and eighth days), 9 .—A sharp cutting pain in the left breast, which
came on at noon, and lasted an hour (third day), 1 *.

Heart and Pulse. —Dull pain in the region of the heart, attended by
dull pain and heaviness in the left upper arm and particularly in the elbow
(fifth day), 8 *.—Deep inspirations are attended by a heavy dull pain in the
region of the heart (sixth day), 8 .—Severe stinging pain in the region of
the heart, extending through the chest to the apex of the left scapula, with
a frequent desire to take a deep inspiration, which increases the pain, in
the afternoon, for two or three hours (second day), 8 *.— [300.] Sharp and
deep pain ascribed to the left side of the heart (third, fourth, and eighth
days), 9 .—Pain in heart (ninth day), 9 .—Palpitation of the heart after sup-

426


per, and after conversation (twelfth day), 0 .—Frequency of heart’s action
greatly increased by going upstairs (fourteenth day), 2 .—Pulse 80 (third
day); 96 (tenth day), 5 .

Neck and Hack .— Sensation as if a thread were tightly tied around
the neck just below the ears, with a slight roaring in the ears (twenty hours
after fourth dose), 8 *.—Pain in the back of the neck (tenth and eleventh
days), 9 .—Pain running down the back (second day), 9 .—Dull and steady
pain in the back (second day), 9 .—Pain in back (fifth day) ; nearly constant
(sixth, seventh, and eighth days), 9 .—[310.] Suffered considerably from
pain in back, in afternoon and evening (tenth day), 2 .—Aching pain in the
back, under and below the apex of the left scapula (fifth day), 8 .—Aching
between the scapulae, while standing (sixth day), 8 .—Pain in middle of back,
for twenty minutes (tenth and eleventh days), 9 .—Stinging-burning pain in
the back, just below the inferior angle of the left scapula; followed and
accompanied by stinging almost itching pain in the left side of the chest,
just below the nipple (after one hour, fourth day), 8 .—Stinging-burning pain
in the back, between the scapulae, attended by a constant desire to take
deep inspirations, with a sensation of dry heat in the middle of the chest
(sixth day), 8 .—Pain under the right scapula; left ditto (third day), 9 .—Pain
in right scapula (first, second, tenth, and eleventh days), 9 .—Pain in left
scapula (ninth day), 9 .—Very sharp pain in left scapula (fifth day), 9 .—
[320.] Pain in the small of the back, for a few minutes (first and second
days), 9 .—Burning pain on a small spot near the top of the right sacro¬
iliac symphysis (after thirteen hours, third day), 8 .—Sore pain at juncture
of th e sacrum with the left ilium, increased by stooping and rising. In a
few hours, this pain became more general in the loins, and appeared like
the pain and lameness following a strain by overlifting. The pain was
increased by a sudden motion of the body, such as from the unexpected
motion of a carriage. At 2 p.m., the lameness somewhat abated, and was
succeeded by a pulsative sensation in the muscles of the nates (fourth
day), 40 .—Aching and sense of great fatigue in the loins (third day), 41 .

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Twitching of right arm and leg (second day). 9 .—Pain
in elbows, arms, and left knee (fourth day), 9 .—Pain in the right arm, hand,
and knee, in the afternoon (fifth day), 9 .—Pain in the right arm, thumb,
and leg; left foot and ankle (sixth day), 9 .—Pain in right arm, thumb, and
knee (seventh day), 9 .—Pain in right arm and knee (eighth day), 9 .—[330.]
Pain in left arm, thumb, and leg (ninth day), 9 .—Pain in the right arm,
hand, and knee (eleventh day), 9 .—Pain in the left arm and foot (eleventh
day), 9 .—Pain in the right arm and legs (twelfth day), 9 .

Superior Extrem ities .—The right arm feels as if its muscles were
glued together and sore to the touch (tenth and following days), 9 .—Slight
numbness and crawling sensation in the left arm, after lying down in bed
(after two hours), 8 .—Soon after waking, left arm feels as if bruised (fifth
day), 9 .—Pain in left arm for two hours, and repeated in fingers of the left
hand (seventh day), 9 .—Pain in left arm, hand, and thumb (eighth day), 9 .
—Pain in left arm and hand, for fifteen minutes (twelfth day), 9 .—[340.]
The shoulders and scapular regions were as often the seats of pain as the
arms, throughout this proving, 9 .—Awoke with pain in right shoulder; it
was ameliorated by rest; passed off in two hours (eleventh day), 2 .—Dull
pain and heaviness in the left upper arm, and particularly in the elbow,
attended the dull pain in the region of the heart (fifth day), 8 *.—Stinging
pain on the inner side of the right upper arm (sixth day), 8 .—Dull aching
in both elbows (after second dose, second day), 8 .—Pain in right wrist, ulnar


427

I

half, 7b .—Pain in left hand (fifth day), 9 .—Pain in the fingers of the left
hand (tenth day), 9 .

Inferior Extremities. — Sense of great lassitude in the lower
limbs, and aching in the calves of the legs, as after long continued walk¬
ing or standing; worse when moving; better when lying down (after six
hours, third day), 48 .—Crawling-tingling sensation in the inferior extremi¬
ties (half an hour after second dose, second day),*; (half an hour after
fourth dose), 81 .— [ 350 .] Legs feel very weak when going up and down stairs,
in the evening (second day), 18 .—Legs feel weak while going up and down
stairs (seventh day) ; in the evening (fourteenth and fifteenth days), 15 .-—
Legs feel weak on going up and down stairs, in the evening (second day), Ic .
—Legs felt weak through the day, especially on going up and down stairs
(twenty-third day), lc .—Weakness of the legs when going up and down stairs
(thirty-fifth day), lc .—Rheumatic pains in legs, dull aching pain in them all
day long (fifth day) ; slight rheumatic pain in afternoon, particularly in right
leg (sixth day), 2 .—In afternoon, feeling of weariness, aching of bones of
lower extremities (second day), 2b .—Aching pain in the right-hip-joint while
walking, producing slight lameness (after thirteen hours, third day), 8 .—
Muscular pain in thighs and legs, slightly increased on pressure (after three
hours, fourth day), 2 .—Pulsative sensation in muscles of nates (fourth day), 41 .
—[ 360 .] Wrenching-aching pain in the flexure of the left knee, while stand¬
ing (twenty-four hours after fourth dose), 8 .—Pain in the knees, very sharp
on rising after sitting awhile, running down the left leg (second day), 9 .—
Drawing pain, almost a cramp, in the calf of the right leg, continued half
an hour (after ten minutes, sixth day), 8 .—Heaviness in the calf of the
right leg, as if the flesh would fall from the bones (a quarter of an hour
after second dose, second day), 8 .—Pain in right leg and toes (ninth day), 9 .
—Pains, rheumatic, in anterior surface of both tibiae, in the evening (tenth
day), 2 .—Rheumatic pains in tibia anteriorly (fifth day), 21 .—Rending in the
anterior part of both ankle-joints, running down the insteps, apparently in
the ligaments; alternating several times with gnawing pain in the internal
condyle of the left humerus ; after which was felt aching and heaviness,
with crawling sensation all through the inferior extremities, when riding
(after four hours, second day), 8 .—Tenderness in the feet, with extreme sen¬
sitiveness and shooting pains in the corns (fourth day), 2 .—Tenderness of
feet (thirteenth day), 28 .— [ 370 .] Pain in left foot, with privation of sensi¬
bility in leg (seventh day), 9 .—Pain in right little toe, especially in corn on
outside of it, 7b .

Generalities .— Great lassitude and weariness, with somnolency ; is
shifting his position constantly; his legs feel tired, though he has done
but little walking to-day (fourth day), 2 .—Great lassitude and uneasiness,
with stagnation of ideas, in the evening (third day), 2 .—A very warm day;
felt languid and weary (third day), 21 .—Felt very weak and tired through
the day (seventh day), 1 *.—Has felt weak during the day (sixth day), lc .—
Sense of great weariness, on going to bed (ninth day), 5 .—* Great languor
(tenth day), 5 .—* Restlessness, in the evening (filth day), 5 .— [ 380 .] The pains
seem to have been neither fixed nor constant anywhere, 9 .—Throbbing
through the whole body (after fifteen hours, fifth day), 8 .—After the seventh
day the distress augmented to such a degree that he was unwilling to con¬
tinue the proving any longer; the evolution of the symptoms continued
after the last dose, from the seventh day to the twenty-second. This prov¬
ing is chiefly characterized by pains, numerous, varied, and of frequent

428


recurrence, from which hardly any part escaped ; these pains were all
transient, one pain ceasing, with complete intermissions of from ten minutes
to an hour, and then another pain coming on; some, of a neuralgic char¬
acter, were so severe, that the prover asked for an antidote, which was re¬
fused ; most of the pains were severe enough to prevent study, hut did not
interfere with active duties. The pains ceased from 11 to 12 A.M., and
recommenced a few hours or less after repeating the dose in the afternoon, 9 .
—* Unusual sensitiveness to cold, during the day (first day), 3 ’.—*Sensitive

lower lip (twelfth day), 5 .—A small vesicle, like a blister, on inside of lower
lip, just beneath the left angle of mouth (seventeenth day'', 2 .—My atten¬

for two or three weeks, gradually increasing until it has become quite a
source of annoyance. It is composed of very abundant minute red pim¬

undressing at night (eighteenth day). The fine eruption on the calves and

scratching; then a multitude of very fine pimples appear. The eruption

surface of the limbs and inner side of the knees (twenty-second day).

tating it by scratching has caused many little pustules, as large as the head
of a large pin. Almost the whole surface of the limbs, from the thighs to
the feet, is covered with this paltry nettlerash, probably a kind of urticaria.

duced, at night (twenty-fourth day). The little sores caused by scratching,

Pupils at one time normal, at another dilated, at another contracted ;
constant trembling of the muscles, at times interrupted by tonic contrac¬
tions, increasing to general clonic spasms, with complete loss of conscious¬

gion, 6 .—Pushing cutting griping, as from flatus, in both sides of the abdo¬
men (after two hours and three-quarters), 7 . — General Abdomen.
Abdomen distended, in the evening (third day), 21 . —Emission of very oflen-
sive flatus (after two hours and a quarter), 7 .—Easy emission of flatus, 6 .
—Emission of flatus, with a sensation as if stool would follow (after thirty-
nine hours), 7 .—Rumbling in the lower abdomen (after one hour), 5 .—Fre¬
quent rumbling and gurgling in the abdomen, 13 .—Heaviness in the abdo¬
men, 13 .— [ 160 . J Griping in the abdomen, with eructations, in the morning,
on rising (fourth day), 2 ' 1 .—Pressure in the abdomen,followed by great empti¬
ness, 13 .—Burning in the abdomen, 13 .—Agreeable coolness in the abdomep
and chest, 6 .—Sticking extending upward in the abdomen whenever she sat
down, 1 .—A tensive pressure in the whole lower abdomen, extending from
the umbilicus downward, at night, as if the menses would come on, aggra¬
vated by pressure, 3 .—Piuching-cuttiug pain, with discomfort, in the lower
abdomen, as after taking cold (after forty-eight hours), 5 . .

Rectum and Anus .— * Tearing in the rectum and urethra, while
urinating (after two days), 2 .— Tearing stitches in the rectum, while sitting, 2 .
—* Frequent pressure for stool, with prolapsus of the rectum, that after this
frequently took place, with a sensation of pressure, also with emission of
much flatus; the slightest stooping, and still more crouching down, caused the
rectum to protrude (after seventy-two hours); for several days afterwards
the rectum remained protruding all the time, and though it could be re¬
duced easily and without pain, yet it immediately protruded again, 2 .—
[ 170 .] Constant desire for stool, which, however, is softer than usual, and
yet after the stool there is dragging and urging (after twenty-four hours),

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
The stool large and evacuated with difficulty, as from loss of
peristaltic action of the rectum, during the first twenty-four hours, 6 .—-A
second soft stool, evacuated with great difficulty on account of a relaxed

436

RUTA.

and inactive condition of the rectum, preceded by a sensation of nausea in
the abdomen (after one hour and a half), 2 .—Soft stool, 12 .—Evacuation of
blood during a stool, 1 .—Stool consisting of a few hard faeces, almost like
sheepdung (after forty hours), 7 .—The stool on the second day was larger
than usual, 2 .

Urinary Organs. —Drawing pressure in the region of the kidneys,
extending along the loins, while sitting, 2 .—Pain over kidneys more marked,
with urgent desire to urinate (after third dose), 22 .—Immediately after urin¬
ating it seems on every step as if the bladder were full and moved up and
down, not while sitting (after forty-eight hours), 3 .— [ 180 .] Pressure in the
region of the neck of the bladder, like a painful closure of it, soon after
urinating (after twenty-four hours), 9 .—* Great pressure to urinate, as though
the bladder were constantly full, yet but little urine is passed, and micturition
is followed by dragging, as though much should be passed, which however does
not occur, for several days (after a few hours), 3 .— *It seems as though she
could no longer hold her water, with an excessively urgent desire, even if there
was only a single drop of urine; during and after micturition very painful
burning in the vagina aud long-continued pressure; during the night, how¬
ever, she could sleep quietly as usual, but in the morning she was obliged
to urinate in the same manner as on the previous day, 3 .—Frequent and
copious micturition, without painful sensation, 12 .—The urine, when passed,
gave a strong odor of rue (after third dose), 22 .—In the aggregate little urine
is pa^ed; after urinating, pressure and dragging in the bladder, without
renewed micturition (second and third days), 2 .—Urine deep-yellow, in the
evening (second day), 21 *.

Sexual Organs. — Male. Nightly emissions, without amorous
dreams, 7 .—Great, increased sexual desire, 3 .— Female. In the evening she
was seized with violent pains, that gradually increased, and were followed
by the discharge of blood from the vagina and miscarriage after forty-eight
hours, 17 .— [ 190 .] Miscarriage of dead children at about seven months; the
uterus was found well contracted; this was followed after two days by vio¬
lent fever and delirium, with spasms, succeeded by great exhaustion and
vomiting of bile; for five days the patient lay in a condition resembling
partial intoxication, with contracted pupils; swollen coated tongue; slight
delirium and very slow pulse, only 30 to the minute, and at times convul¬
sive spasms of the arms; vomiting and painful tension in the epigastric
region ; the abdomen was soft and painless; the uterus contracted, though
the lochise soon ceased to flow; after awhile the lochise returned ; the patient
gradually recovered, though she was very weak for a long time, aud the
great slowness of the pulse continued for many days, 18 .—Miscarriage oc¬
curred on the sixth day, followed by a long slow recovery, 19 .

Respiratory Organs. —Pain, as from a blow or bruise, in the
larynx, 6 .—Forcible cough, in the evening, immediately after lying dowm,
with much expectoration of stringy mucus; the cough returned several
times at night, but only for a short time and less violently; when the cough
was very violent, it seemed as if the stomach turned over and as if he would
vomit, 12 .— *He was awakened about midnight by a choking cough, with scrap¬
ing in the upper part of the chest, without pain, and with a slight infrequent
expectoration, 12 .—Dyspnoea and shortness of breath, 12 .

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
A pressive fulness in the chest, that causes dyspnoea and short¬
ness of breath, 1 .—Stitches in the chest and arrest of breathing, that caused
great anxiety on ascending steps, 2 .—Hard pressure on the sixth true rib,
aggravated on expiration aud on touch (after two hours), 5 .—Violent pres-

RUTA.

437

sure in the lower part of the chest, by the last false ribs, at night; he
dreamed that some one was encircling him tightly, on which account he
woke (after twenty-four hours), 9 .—[200.] An intermittent gnawing or pick¬
ing on one of the costal cartilages, above the ensiform cartilage, at night, 9 .
—Internal heat in the chest and abdomen, 6 .—Burning stitches in the chest,
especially beneath the sternum, like pains in an ulcer (second morning), 21 .
—Agreeable coolness in the chest, 6 .— * Pressure on the sternum, seeming to
he internal and external , 5 .—Pressive oppressive stitches on the sternum dur¬
ing both inspiration and expiration, while sitting (after four hours), 7 .—
Stitches in the sternum on every motion (second day), 2 .— Gnawing pain,
associated with some biting and burning, in the right side of the chest /'.—
Tremulous bubbling in the last true ribs of the right side (after a quarter
of an hour), 9 .—Aching beneath the left short ribs, aggravated on pressure
and taking away the breath, on waking at night, 3 .—[210.] Gnawing in the
left side of the chest, 6 . — Corrosive biting drawing in the left side of the chest, 6 .
—Dull thrusts in the left side of the chest, 6 .—A fine painful throbbing or
picking beneath the left short ribs, 3 .—Violent stitches between the left
nipple and axilla, aggravated by inspiration (after thirty hours), 5 .—Stick¬
ing pain externally in the left nipple, aggravated by inspiration (after four
days), 5 .

Pulse .—Pulse moderately accelerated, 18 .—Pulse increased in frequency
(after third dose), 22 .—Pulse very small and slow, 19 .

Neck and Pack. — Neck. Drawing in the nape of the neck, 8 .—
[220.] Stiffness of the neck, in the morning (third day), 4 .— *Pain, as if
sprained or bruised, in the nape and shoulders (second day ), 2I \—Burning in
the neck, below the left ear, about 10 a.m. (fifth day), 211 .—Fine cutting
extending from the neck to the chest, especially on the clavicle and in the
axilla, where it continues, while walking; aggravated by walking rapidly
(after thirty-six hours), 9 . — Pack. *Bruised pain extending along the back,
especially in the left side, while sitting (after seven hours and three-quar¬
ters ), 7 .—^* Drawing bruised pain in the spine, frequently taking away the
breath/. —Bruised pain on the left side of the back while sitting, disappear¬
ing on walking and standing (after ten hours and a half), 7 .— *Pain in back
(after second dose), 22 .—*Pain, as if beaten and lame, in the spine, 6 .—Pain
in the back, with heaviness in the limbs, disappearing after a little exer¬
tion, in the evening (second day), 211 .—[230.] *The spine is painfid, as if
beaten, while sitting and walking, a pain that takes away the breath /.—
Stitches in the spine, with sudden anxiety, while sitting, 2 .— Dorsal.
Pressure on the right scapula internally (after fourteen hours), 5 .—Pressure
between the scapulae, in the afternoon (fourth day), 211 .—*Pressive-draw T ing
very acute pain in the right side of the spine, opposite the liver, especially
on inspiration (after two days), 2 .—Pressure on the right scapula, with shiv¬
ering (second day), 21 *.— Painful jerking in the spine, opposite the pit of the
stomach ; on pressure of the hand it is more violent, and associated with
an aching beneath the last short ribs, that extends into the abdomen and
impedes lespiration, 9 .—Drawing pain in the scapulae, impeding respiration, 2 .
— *Pain, as from a fall, in the dorsal vertebrae, during rest and motion, 6 .—
Drawing-sticking pain on the tip of the scapula on moving it, so that he
was obliged to let the arm hang down, 2 .—[240.] Sticking and pressure
starting from the angle of the scapula and extending to the back (second
day), 2 ’ 1 .—Sticking itching between the scapulae, not relieved by rubbing
(immediately), 9 .— Lumbar. Awakened at 4 a.m. by a violent tearing
pain in the small of the back, that disappeared only about 9 a.m., 12 . —

438

RUTA.

* Pain, as if bruised, in the lumbar vertebrae, 6 . —A digging, as if bruised, in
the lumbar region, just above the small of the back, while sitting (after a
long walk); on walking, it continues for some time, gradually disappear¬
ing; it returns while standing still and while sitting, 3 .—Tearing pulling-
sticking pains in the small of the back (first day), 21 *.—Intermittent painful
bfeatiug in the back, just above the left ilium, during rest and motion ; re¬
lieved by pressure, but returning afterwards, 3 .—Pain in the posterior pro¬
cess of the ilium, even while sitting, like a forcing forward, and a sensation
as if something were pressed outward ; always relieved by pressure, 1 .—
Hard pressure on the left side of the ilium, near the spine (after two hours'),’.
—An intermittent beating in the anterior spine of the left ilium, 3 .—(230.]
A beating on the posterior margin of the left ilium, that extends over the
hip to the interior surface of the thigh and down almost to the knee, and
disappearing when pressing upon the ilium (after a long walk), 3 .—Hard
pressure on the left lower portion of the sacrum, 5 .— *Pain, as from a blow
or fall, extending from the coccyx to the sacrum, 6 .

Extremities* —Constant, not convulsive, motions of the limbs, 19 .—
All the limbs are heavy, weary, and without strength ; all work seems too
great; she is averse to it, 1 .—Weakness of the limbs while sitting; he is not
willing to move them ; when he lays the hands upon the lap, they are so
comfortable that he does not wish to raise them, 4 .—The hands and feet are
powerless; she can hold nothing firmly in the hands, and when walking
cannot stand firmly upon the feet, 1 .—Heaviness of the limbs, without sweat
(second day), 21 *.—Pressive cramplike tearing now in the upper, now in the
lower limbs, during rest and motion (after three hours and a half), 7 .— He
is unable to bend on account of pains in all the joints and hip-bones (after ten
hours), 6 .

Superior Extremities. — [ 260 .] Acute pain, as from a sprain, in
the shoulder-joint, somewhat relieved on drawing and turning the arm up¬
ward, but immediately returning on allowing the arm to hang down or to
lie upon anything, 6 .—Paiu, as if sprained, in the right shoulder (third day), 21 .
—Pain, as from a burning-biting ulcer, in the right axilla (after forty-eight
days), 6 .—Stitches in the shoulders (fourth day), 218 .—Painful jerks in the
upper arms, commencing at the middle ; when the pain reaches the elbow,
it extends down to the fingers and seems to be in the long bones, with weari¬
ness and heaviness of the lower extremities, 3 .—Dull tearing in the humeri
(after an hour), 9 .—Cramplike drawing in the biceps muscles, 2 .—Hard pres¬
sure.in the elbow-joint, aggravated on stretching out the arm (after twelve
hours), 5 .—Pain, as from a blow, in the left elbow-joint, with weakness of
the arm (after thirty-six hours), 6 .—Dull tearing pain in the right elbow-
joint and neighboring parts, extending to the lower extremity of the hu¬
merus; on stretching out the arm it is rather a pressive pain (after thirty-
six hours), 5 .— [ 270 .] The ulna seems bruised, 6 .—Painful pressive drawing
in the middle of the anterior surface of the right forearm (after thirty-four
hours), 5 .—Paralytic pressure on the upper portion of the right forearm
(after ten hours), 5 .—Cramplike tearing in the left forearm, 7 .—Tearing pres¬
sure in the right wrist, aggravated by violent motion (after thirty-two
hours), 5 .—Pain, as if broken, in the left wrist, even during rest, 6 .—Veins
of the hands swollen after eating (after four hours), 6 .— The bones in the
wrist and back of the hand are 'painful, as if bruised, during rest and motion, 6 .
—Cramplike pain transversely across the hands (after seven hours), 7 .—
Fine sticking-itching tingling in the palm of the left hand (after thirty-six
hours), 7 .— [ 280 .] Pressive drawing in the middle joints of the three right

RUTA.

439

middle finger?, 5 .—A painful pressive drawing in the last joints of the two
last fingers, at night (after forty-two hours), 5 .—Tearing in the middle fin¬
ger, especially in the middle joint and middle phalanx (after three-quarters
of an hour), 5 .—Sore and ulcerative pain in the left ring finger (second
day), 21 .—Pain, as from a blow or bruise, in the fingers during rest (after,
six hours), 6 .

Inferior Extremities. — Gait unsteady (after third dose), 22 .—
Great weakness in the lower extremities; walking was very difficult; it
seemed as though a heavy weight were hanging to the legs, 12 .— *On rising
after sitting he cannot walk at first; he falls back again; the bones seem
broken ; the thighs refuse their service on account of powerlessness and
pain, 6 .—While walking, he staggers from side to side, 6 .— While walking, he
falls from side to side; the feet will not stipport him; there is no power nor
steadiness in the thighs, 6 . —[290.] A bruised pain in the legs, with tight
tension across the lower abdomen, only while sitting, not while walking
and standing, 3 .—Tremulous heaviness of the legs, 6 .— Ascending a hill as
well as descending is difficult ; the legs give out, 6 . — Hip* * Pain, as from a
blow or fall, in the bones aboid the hips (during motion), 6 .—* The painful
parts, especially the hips and bones of the legs, are sore, as if beaten, whenever
touched (after twenty-nine hours), 6 .— Thigh. * The posterior portion of the
thigh above the knee seems bruised (during motion), 6 .— *The whole anterior
surface of the thigh feels bruised and painf ul to touch (after thirty-one hours), 6 .
—* Bruised pain in the thigh continues two days; he can scarcely walk, 6 .—
* Whenever he stretches out the limbs, even a little, the thighs are painful, as if
beaten to pieces, 6 .— Hard pressure in the middle of the outer portion of the
left thigh, 5 .—r300.] Hard pressure on the upper and inner surface of the
left thigh, 5 .—Pressure in the middle of the outer portion of the right thigh, 5 .
—At night pain in both the thighs, as though the parts were violently
grasped and squeezed by the hands, 12 .—(A violent contractive and spas¬
modically drawing pain extending from the middle of the thigh to the hip-
joint and thence to the small of the back), 1 .—Sharp burning pressure in
the bend of the right thigh (after one hour), 5 .—A burning pain on the
upper aud inner surfaces of the thighs only while sitting, and especially on
waking, while lying in bed, not while standing or walking, 1 .—Pain in the
middle of the femurs, as if beaten (during motion), 6 .—Cramplike throbbing
pain in the middle at first of the right, afterwards of both thighs at the
same time; after this had disappeared a similar pain on the outer side of
the left leg, below the knee, that soon in turn disappeared, 12 .— Knee.
Trembling of the knees, with weakness of the feet, 8 .—Sinking down of the
knees on rising from a seat and beginning to walk (after four hours), 6 .—
[310.] Weariness of the left knee after walking a little; the knees give
way, 3 .—Paralytic heaviness in the knees; he is obliged to change the posi¬
tion of the feet (after one hour) ; after walking he has relief', 9 .—Sticking,
as if ulcerated, above the right knee while standing aud walking (second
day), 21 .—Spasmodic contractions in the hollows of the knees on rising from
a seat, 6 .— A nkle. A pain, consisting of a throbbing and hacking, as if there
was an ulcer on the anterior portion of the left ankle, 6 . —Burning sensation
beneath the external malleolus while standing, 2 .— Foot. Painful pressure
in the sole of the left foot while sitting (after thirty-six hours), 7 .—Pressive-
sticking pain first in the left, then in the right heel (while sitting), (after
twelve hours), 7 .— He does not dare to step heavily upon the feet, on account of
pains in the bones of the feet, with a sensation of heat 6 . —Cramp in the sole
of the left foot (second day), 2]a .—[320.] Dull stitches shoot slowly from

440

RUTA.

the back of the foot up the tibia (after half an hour), 9 .— Burning and biting
pains in the bones of the feet during rest,''. — Toes. Burning paius in the
toes, as after a bruise or blow, where a foreign body had been forced in, 6 .
—Burning tearing in the left great toe, especially on external pressure
(after six hours), 9 .—Painful drawing in the toes, 6 .—Fine cramplike stitches
in the right little toe (while sitting), that become violent and piercing on
moving tbe toes (after three hours), 1 .

Generalities. —The patient looks intoxicated ; the eyes and face
red, 18 .— * Great weakness after a short walk; the limbs feel bruised; the
small of Ihe back and loins are painful, yet he experiences the symptoms
only after sitting down ; on rising and walking about he seems better, 3 .—
Unusually weak (sleepy) in the afternoon, disappearing after walking
(second day), 21 *. — Weakness, in the morning (second day), 21 *.— [330.]
Unusually weary very soon after playing with the children, in the evening
(second day), 21 *.—Great weariness and heaviness of the whole body after a
meal; such sleepiness that the eyes close; better in the open air, 3 .—Great
weariness, 8 .—Weariness and indolence only while sitting, not iu the least
after walking awhile, 4 .—Lassitude and heaviness of the whole body, 6 .—
Great prostration, 19 .—Faintness, 19 .—Occasional feeling of faintness (after
second dose), 22 .—Great restlessness three evenings in succession, with pres-
sive headache and feverish heat, 2 .—Restlessness, 10 .— [340.] Indescribable
6ense of nervousness, creating a fear that an overdose had been taken (after
third dose), 22 .— He does not know where to lay his legs on account of uneasi¬
ness and heaviness; he lies now in one place, now in another, and turns from
side to side, 6 .—* All parts of the body upon which he lies, even in bed, are
painful, as if bruised (after seventeen hours), 6 .—The whole body seems
pressed full, associated with impeded respiration, 1 .

SItill. — Eruptions • Corrodes the skin and draws blisters,".f—Pap¬
ular eruption on the upper and lower lips (from vinegar of Rue), 11 .—After
touching it for some time, the skin becomes inflamed and the hands swell, 15 .
—Erysipelas of the hands and forehead, 16 .—Erysipelas of the hands, 10 .J—
Very acute itching on the hands, which became red; after some hours
there developed vesicles filled with transparent liquid, and surrounded by
a very red areola; these vesicles were more numerous between the fingers
than on the rest of the hand; they showed a general disposition to become
clustered, and were somewhat like the pustules occasioned by the itch in¬
sect ; on the next day, the itching became very violent, the vesicles com¬
pletely covered both hands, the itching was almost intolerable, especially
at night; when the vesicles became confluent, very large phlyctenules de¬
veloped and resembled an incomplete vesication by cantharides; this con¬
dition persisted ten or twelve days, after which the inflammation subsided
and the hands desquamated. Even after three weeks small vesicles con¬
tinued to appear in the palms of the hands, and were disposed to form
groups, as if caused by the bites of insects. Very great itching developed
on the great toes, and a crop of vesicles identical with those between the
hands ; this eruption on the feet was certainly not caused by direct contact
of Rue, but resulted from the infection of the hands, and did not occur
until several days after the trouble commenced on the hands. The next
year the same man came again iu contact with the leaves ; the effects were
more intense than before; for three months the hauds seemed denuded of
skin, they looked as if they had been boiled, and were completely excori-

I From the application of the herb.

J Caused by application of the herb.

RUTA.

441

ated ; there was also intense fever, keeping the patient in bed five or six
days, 20 .— [350.] Next morning he observed that both his hands were re¬
markably red and warm ; on the third day the redness and pain had in¬
creased to such an extent that the sensation was as if both hands had been
exposed to scalding vapors; he rubbed them gently with sweet oil; towards
evening they were densely covered with water blisters, especially at the
tips of the fingers, which had been most exposed to the pollen ; on the
fourth day the swelling of the hands still continued to a considerable ex¬
tent, between the blisters they showed a dark-red color with a bluish tinge;
on the fifth and sixth days the swelling likewise spread over the posterior
surface of the arm as far as the elbow; embrocations of Chamomile and
Elderflowers were applied, and the blisters were opened ; within the space
of four weeks the epidermis of the hands gradually peeled off, even in
localities where no blisters had existed, 14 .— Sensations. Itching about
the corners of the mouth (third day), 21 .—Formication on the thigh, so that
he was obliged to scratch the side upon which he was not lying, 13 .—Deep
fine stitches very close together in both arms that change to a kind of biting
itching, with redness and heat of the skin of the arm, 1 .—Hot tingling
prickling in the soles of the feet, 6 .—* Itching over the whole body , relieved by
scratching , in the morning on rising from bed (after twenty-four hours), 7 .—
Itching on one side of the face (after twenty-four hours), 2 .—Itching of the
left upper arm, provoking scratching (after eight hours), 7 .

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Yawning and stretching in the house, followed by sleepiness, 6 .—
Yawning (incompletely) several times, that is not satisfying; in the midst
of yawning he was obliged to stop, 4 .— [360.] Yawning, with fever, 15 .—
Much yawning, especially at night, even after eating (first day), 21 *.—Yawn¬
ing, with stretching of the arms and legs, especially of the former, 4 .—Great
sleepiness, after eating, 13 .—Sleepy, in the forenoon, 13 .—Overpowered by
sleep, heavy, the head seems befogged (second day'), 21 .—She fell so soundly
asleep, immediately on lying down in the evening, that it was difficult to
arouse her, 3 .—Excessive sleepiness after eating; he fell asleep while read¬
ing; sleep with partial consciousness; he awoke with a cry of extreme
fright on the slightest touch, 8 .—Starting up in fright and jerking the feet,
during the afternoon nap, 13 .—She tossed from side to side in extreme unea¬
siness, woke nearly every hour, and could with difficulty fall asleep again, 7 .
— [370.] During night but little sleep, and great restlessness (after third
dose), 22 .—Night sleep restless ; he was obliged to lie here and there, with¬
out heat of the body or cough, or any thought that prevented sleep; he
was obliged to rise three times to urinate, and passed an unusually large
amount of urine, 12 .—Uneasy sleep, with fretful morose dreams, 6 .—Unre¬
freshing sleep, from 3 to 4 A.M., afterwards inability to sleep, with heavi¬
ness of the head (fifth day), 21 *.—Uneasiness at night; she awoke frequently,
had nausea and painful twisting about the umbilicus; at times it seemed
as though something rose to the pit of the throat, and as if water would
accumulate in the mouth, 3 .—Awake a long time at night, internal confu¬
sion of the head, without special pain, prevents his falling asleep (third
day), 2U .— Frequent waking at night as if it were time to rise, 1 . — Vivid con¬
fused dreams,\ —Constant fatiguing dreams, at night (fourth day), 21 *.—
Vivid dreams during sleep (first night), 21 *.— [380.] Dreamy sleep, vivid
dreams (first night), 21 .

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilliness . Chilliness or rather shaking chill over the
whole body, with gooseflesh, associated with yawning and stretching, 4 .—
Frequent chilliness and shuddering during the day (first day), 21 *.—Chilli-

442

RUTA.

ness and coldness of the whole body, 8 .—Internal chilliness; she could not
get warm (a sensation that she always experienced just before the appear¬
ance of the menses), 3 .—Shivering of the whole body, even by a warm
stove; the hands and feet feel cold, with internal and external warmth of
the face and dulness of the head, as in catarrhal fever, with thirst, which
disappeared after drinking once, though it had been very violent before, 3 .—
Creeping coldness over half the head and face, 6 .—Coldness creeps over
him, especially up the back, 12 .—General coldness of the extremities, 19 .—
Shivering over the back and chest, 6 .— [390.] Sensation of coldness running
up and down the back, 6 .— Coldness down the spine, 6 . —Internal coldness in
the arms, 6 .—Hands and feet cold (fourth day), 21 \—A sensation of internal
coldness, almost like falling asleep, on the inner side of the leg, from the
sole of the foot to the knee, without shivering (after twenty-four hours), 1 .—
Heat. Fever, with yawning, 15 .—Flushes of heat over the body (after
three doses), 22 .—Heat over the whole body, and feverish restlessness, with
anxiety, as though he would die, that took away his breath, and great heat,
especially of the face, without thirst, with white-coated tongue, that seemed
red and dry, in the afternoon, 2 .—Heat all over, 1 .—Temperature somewhat
elevated, 18 . —[400.] Great heat in the head, with feverish restlessness of the
whole body and anxiety (about 11 p.m.), 2 .— Heat in the head, 6 . — Increased
warmth of the face, 6 .—Internal and external heat of the face with redness, 6 .—•
Sweat. Sweat broke out over the whole body, after walking in the open
air (after six hours), 6 .—Sweat, while walking in the open air, in the after¬
noon (third day), 21 .—Perspiration on the crown of the head (immediately), 1 .
—(Cold sweat on the face, in the morning in bed, with redness of the
cheeks), 1 .—Slight perspiration on the back of the nose; the nose and also
the cheeks are warmer than natural, with slight redness of the face, with¬
out thirst, 3 .

Conditions .—Aggravation.— (Morning), On rising from bed, ver¬
tigo; after rising, headache; on waking, dulness in brain ; mucus in can-
thi; pressure in pit of stomach; on rising, itching; in bed, cold sweat.—*
(Afternoon), Ill-humored; thirst for cold water.— (Evening), Ill-humored ;
on going to sleep, dulness in brain ; while reading, sensation of heat in
eyes ; after lying down, cough ; restlessness.— (Night), Pressure in pit of
stomach ; pressure in lower abdomen ; emissions; pressure in lower part of
chest; gnawing on costal cartilage ; drawing in last two joints of last two
fingers; pain in thighs; uneasiness.— (Open air), Pressure on the inner
surface of right eye, with lachrymation.— (Brushing or pieicing teeth), Bleed¬
ing of gums.—( When coughing). Pain over forehead.— (After eating), Veins
of hand swollen ; sleepiness.— (Expiration), Pressure on sixth true rib.—
(Inserting finger), Pressure in ear.— (Inspiration), Stitches between left
nipple and axilla; pain in left nipple.— (After a meal), Weariness and
